text:
Marathon Petroleum jumped 3.2% today, recovering much of what it had lost over the past two weeks. The move follows a sharp reversal in oil market sentiment: after crude briefly dipped below $90 a barrel on Monday on hopes for a near-term end to the Iran conflict, prices have rebounded sharply—US crude is now at $99.64 and Brent at $107.03. Refiners like Marathon benefit directly when oil prices rise, since they buy crude cheap and sell refined products (gasoline, diesel) at prices that don't fall as fast, widening their profit margins.

The rebound reflects growing skepticism about a quick diplomatic resolution. While Trump said Tuesday that an Iran war would end "fairly soon," Secretary of State Rubio signaled the same day that negotiations remain stuck, and reports of escalating Iranian threats suggest the conflict may not resolve as cleanly as the market briefly hoped on Monday. That uncertainty has pushed oil prices back up, which is supporting refiner margins.
